source_checks.conclusion: Runtime retains the same Process/Files/Desktop Arc allocations used as each static ABI factory seed. The factory downcasts the seed; it does not construct duplicate native state.

Local reference expansion, attachment import, completion, resource reads and desktop handoff delegate to the same previously granted state. Constructor roots and context_roots are unchanged; no new remote bypass is registered.

Process owns nine provider routes but emits only four default catalogs. The optional five are omitted, not replaced by empty catalogs. Registry replacement is provider-scoped and identical descriptors preserve generations. Existing optional registrations are not erased by Runtime construction.

Core validation, before/after hook, audit and output guard remain in Runtime. Host rechecks the exact provider/native-name/generation route before admission, after the queue and immediately before ABI start; Process checks the same stamp. HarnessCall shares its original Arc and REQUEST_ID is restored on the local executor; no AUDIT_RUN binding is serialized.

ABI Outcome retains Result<Value,String>; native MCP isError/images/opaque metadata are not rewrapped or silently truncated by the host. ABI and cleanup errors reach Runtime cleanup audit rather than successful tool results.

Stop signal is independent of queue capacity. Queued calls are rejected, active ABI tasks are cancelled/dropped and drained, and real plugin shutdown runs before instance/LocalSet/runtime destruction and completion notification. Shared lazy initialization intentionally outlives a cancelled waiter, then aborts and drains during Process shutdown, matching the original contract.

limits: This is source review; it does not substitute for the parent-owned focused tests or actual CLI lifecycle tests.
Parent reports cargo check --locked --lib --tests passed on this head without warnings; this review did not invoke Cargo.

Process Driver/Shell/Terminal shutdown return types and bounded shell wait were inherited. A successful Process cleanup value is not a new proof that every external tool reported an error-free shutdown.
The inherited Linux Managed Drop path requests guardian termination and uses an independent std-thread watchdog; the native host runtime is kept alive through explicit plugin cleanup.
